        "content": "[\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"47857\",\n    \"score\": 0.6501227021217346,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Profile: Who is steel tycoon Ahmed Ezz?\\ndate: 2018-03-03\\n---\\nCAIRO \\u2013 3 March 2018: Having reconciled with the Egyptian state after seven years of lawsuits, steel tycoon and politician Ahmed Ezz, known for his Mubarak-era corruption and embezzlement cases, is our spotlight guest.\\n\\nEzz was born to an Egyptian father, Lieutant Abdel Aziz Ezz, and a Palestinian mother, Afaf Halawa, in 1959; into a family that had \\\"traded building materials for generations,\\\" according to The Washington Post. Later on, when Ezz would become a political and economic tycoon in Egyptian society, his opposition would manipulate his background to claim that his mother was Jewish, which should disallow him from joining and playing in Egyptian politics, Sky News Arabia stated.\\n\\nThe tycoon had taken to walking with an air of superiority from a young age; he gained a strong sense of self-esteem when he began excelling at school, Sky News Arabia explained. Ezz was enrolled in one of Egypt's leading international schools in the 1960s, and that had already guaranteed him an imbalanced playing field.\\n\\nThis would later on become a strong basis for the Egyptian public hating him \\u2013 or wishing they were him.\\n\\n\\\"With a curt wave of her hand, the wife of one of Egypt's richest men poses a question she already knows the answer to. 'Who is sympathetic to the billionaire?' Abla Ezz asks. 'No one,'\\\" The Washington Post wrote in 2011.\\n\\nBut from an early age, Ezz took a strong interest in his father's business. He would supervise their outlet in the local area of Al Sabteya.\\n\\nHis father left the Egyptian army after the 1967 Naksa; at the time when the Egyptian government were carrying out a purging campaign on the army. Even though he wasn't liable for losing the war, Ezz's father was still barred, Sky News Arabia mentioned. Yet, his father's close ties to late President Gamal Abdel Nasser garnered him a monthly 40-ton share in the country's steel to distribute. Quite a substantial amount at the time.\\n\\nYet The Washington Post reports that many of his defenders would argue that the tycoon was \\\"self-made\\\" even though evidence points to the contrary.\\n\\n\\\"Ezz's defenders say he deserved all the money he earned and came by it\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"72355\",\n    \"score\": 0.640318751335144,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Ahmed Ezz - Wikipedia\\ndate: 2016-02-13\\n---\\nAhmed Ezz may refer to:\\n\\n* Ahmed Ezz (actor) (born 1971), Egyptian actor\\n* Ahmed Ezz (businessman) (born 1959), Egyptian businessman and politician\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"56191\",\n    \"score\": 0.5306457877159119,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Egyptian billionaire Ahmed Ezz spends $11.1 million to boost stake in Ezz Steel\\nauthor: Omokolade Ajayi\\ndate: 2023-12-22\\n---\\nTable of Contents\\n\\nEgyptian billionaire businessman Ahmed Ezz, founder of leading steelmaker Ezz Steel, has further solidified his control over the company by snapping up additional shares in a deal worth EGP344 million ($11.1 million).\\n\\nThe transaction, brokered by Hermes Financial Group, saw Ezz acquire roughly 4.3 million shares at an average price of EGP80 ($2.59) per share from fellow Egyptian steel magnate Jamal El-Garhy \\u2014 this strengthens Ezz's position as the majority shareholder.\\n\\nLatest purchase strengthens Ezz's grip\\n\\nEzz Steel \\u2014 the largest independent steel producer in the Middle East and North Africa \\u2014 has delivered impressive financial results in recent times, further strengthening investors' interest and confidence. With a total output of 5.14 million metric tonnes, Ezz Steel is far ahead of Saudi Arabia's Hadeed and Emirates Steel.\\n\\nPrior to the transaction, Ezz held a commanding 60.71-percent stake. Mineral Investment Development and El-Garhy Steel Group followed with 7.44 percent and 5.93 percent, respectively. The latest purchase strengthens Ezz's grip, solidifying his position as the group's dominant shareholder.\\n\\nEzz Steel dominates MENA market with stellar financial performance\\n\\nEzz Steel's financial performance in the first nine months of 2023 has been nothing short of impressive. Profits soared to EGP27.9 billion ($883.1 million), a significant jump from the previous year's EGP22.1 billion ($709.6 million). Sales followed suit, surging from EGP60.6 billion ($1.96 billion) to EGP103.2 billion ($3.34 billion) \\u2013 a 70-percent increase year-over-year.\\n\\nEzz's latest acquisition comes on the heels of a significant surge in Ezz Steel's share price on the Egyptian Exchange. Between Nov. 1 and 22, the market value of his existing stake climbed by EGP1.77 billion ($57.53 million), solidifying his position as both a leading investor on the bourse and one of the country's wealthiest individuals.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"90680\",\n    \"score\": 0.5291353464126587,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Asad Ahmed - Wikipedia\\ndate: 2007-10-02\\n---\\nname: Asad Ahmed\\nnative_name: \\u0627\\u0633\\u062f \\u0627\\u062d\\u0645\\u062f\\nnative_name_lang: ur\\nbirth_date: 21 July 1971\\nbirth_place: Karachi, Pakistan\\norigin: Karachi, Pakistan\\noccupation: Musician, Songwriter, Record producer, Entrepreneur\\ngenre: Hard rock, heavy metal\\ninstrument: Guitar\\ncurrent_member_of: KaravanAwazVital Signs\\nyears_active: 1987 \\u2013 present\\n\\nAsad Ahmed (born 21 July 1971) is a Pakistani guitarist. He has been a member of various musical groups and some of the earliest Pakistani rock bands like The Barbarians, Awaz, Karavan, Junoon, Vital Signs and Coke Studio Pakistan.\\n\\nEarly life\\n\\nHis family moved to Dubai when he was quite young. His elder brother was a guitarist and when he left for college, he left his guitar back at home. Asad picked it up and quickly learned to play. His family returned to Karachi in 1984.\\n\\nPersonal life\\n\\nOn 14 February 2019, Ahmed married Hira after dating her for two years. They got married in a nikah ceremony surrounded by close family and friends in Karachi.\\n\\nCareer\\n\\nCoke Studio (Pakistan)\\n\\nAsad played in Coke Studio (Produced by Rohail Hyatt) and was one of the house band members from season 2 (2008) to season 6 (2012) and reappeared in Season 13 in 2020. His style of guitar playing has some flashy showmanship in it.\\n\\nThe Barbarians\\n\\nAsad started his music career in 1987 with The Barbarians, which is regarded by many as Pakistan's first rock band. The band's first single \\\"Yeh Zindagi Hai\\\" (This is Life) set the foundation of Pakistani rock. \\n\\nThey released their only album, the self-titled \\\"The Barbarians\\\" in 1989 with the label EMI (Pakistan), which did not fare well in the then rock-repellant Pakistani music industry. The Barbarians band fell apart in 1990.\\n\\nJunoon and Vital Signs\\n\\nAsad did a gig with Salman Ahmad of Junoon at a party in 1991. On Salman's invitation, he hopped on board with Junoon\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"86230\",\n    \"score\": 0.5112382769584656,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Ahmed Ezz takes direct controlling stake in Ezz Steel\\ndate: 2021-06-08\\n---\\n\\nAhmed Ezz now directly owns a controlling stake in Ezz Steel after purchasing a 33.4% stake in the company from El Ezz Group Holding for Industry and Investment, according to an EGX disclosure (pdf). He was ordered to pay back the money, as well as additional damages of double that amount.\\n\\nHis trial over further charges of profiteering and illegally seizing public funds has been postponed until Tuesday 31 October.\\n\\nThe prosecution will accuse Ezz of making a deal with former Minister of Industry Ibrahim Mohamedeen. The former minister allegedly allowed Ezz to illegally take over the state-owned Dekheila steel company.\\n\\nEzz was a prominent figure in former President Hosni Mubarak's now defunct NDP. He was head of the organisation committee and was the architect of the 2010 parliamentary elections that gave the party a 99 percent super majority.\\n\\nHe was also one of the closest allies to Mubarak's son, Gamal, and the two were viewed as the defining figures of the \\\"new guard\\\" within the party.\\n\\nThrough the policies committee of the party, of which the younger Mubarak was chairman and Ezz a member, the two steered the government into adopting aggressive neoliberal policies of free market capitalism, with the state selling off most of the companies nationalised in the 1960s by late President Gamal Abdel Nasser.\\n\\nDespite his advocacy for free market policies, Ezz, who was also a member of the lower house of parliament, the People's Assembly, has long been accused of holding a monopoly on the steel market.\"\n  }\n]"

(Photo by Ayman Aref\\\\/NurPhoto via Getty Images)\\\",\\\"image_credit\\\":\\\"Ayman Aref\\\\/NurPhoto\\\\/Getty Images\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"31823\",\n    \"score\": 0.4659988284111023,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Abdel Halim Hafez - Wikipedia\\nauthor: Authority control databases\\ndate: 2005-10-03\\n---\\nname: Abdel Halim Hafez\\u0639\\u0628\\u062f \\u0627\\u0644\\u062d\\u0644\\u064a\\u0645 \\u062d\\u0627\\u0641\\u0638\\nhonorific_prefix: ORE\\nbirth_name: Abdel Halim Ali Shabana\\u0639\\u0628\\u062f \\u0627\\u0644\\u062d\\u0644\\u064a\\u0645 \\u0639\\u0644\\u064a \\u0634\\u0628\\u0627\\u0646\\u0629\\nbirth_date: 21 June 1929\\nbirth_place: El-Halawat, El Sharqia, Kingdom of Egypt\\ndeath_date: 30 03 1977\\ndeath_place: London, England\\ngenre: Egyptian music, Classical Arabic Music\\noccupations: Singer, actor, music teacher, conductor, film producer\\nyears_active: 1952\\u20131977\\nlabel: Mazzika\\n\\nAbdel Halim Ali Shabana (), commonly known as Abdel Halim Hafez (, ) (21 June 1929 \\u2013 30 March 1977), was an Egyptian singer, actor, conductor, businessman, music teacher and film producer.\\n\\nAbdel Halim is considered to be one of the greatest Egyptian musicians of his era, along with Umm Kulthum, Mohamed Abdel Wahab, Farid Al Atrach, Mohamed Fawzi, and Shadia. As his popularity grew, he was given the nickname 'el-Andaleeb el-Asmar (), meaning The Dark-Skinned Nightingale. He achieved extraordinary success as a popular musician throughout the Arab world, with estimated sales of over 80 million records.\\n\\nEarly life\\n\\nBorn Abdel Halim Ali Shabanah in El-Halawat in El Sharqia, 80 kilometers (50 miles) north of Cairo, he was the fourth child of Ali Ismail Shabanah. He had two brothers, Ismail and Mohamed, and one sister, Alyah. His mother died from labor complications three days after giving birth to him \\u2013 something that made people around him believe that he brought bad luck. His father died as well a few months later, leaving him and his siblings orphaned at a young age. He lived in a poor orphanage for a number of years. With a total output of 5.14 million metric tonnes, Ezz Steel is far ahead of Saudi Arabia's Hadeed and Emirates Steel.\\n\\nPrior to the transaction, Ezz held a commanding 60.71-percent stake. Mineral Investment Development and El-Garhy Steel Group followed with 7.44 percent and 5.93 percent, respectively. The latest purchase strengthens Ezz's grip, solidifying his position as the group's dominant shareholder.\\n\\nEzz Steel dominates MENA market with stellar financial performance\\n\\nEzz Steel's financial performance in the first nine months of 2023 has been nothing short of impressive. He was ordered to pay back the money, as well as additional damages of double that amount.\\n\\nHis trial over further charges of profiteering and illegally seizing public funds has been postponed until Tuesday 31 October.\\n\\nThe prosecution will accuse Ezz of making a deal with former Minister of Industry Ibrahim Mohamedeen. The former minister allegedly allowed Ezz to illegally take over the state-owned Dekheila steel company.\\n\\nEzz was a prominent figure in former President Hosni Mubarak's now defunct NDP. He was head of the organisation committee and was the architect of the 2010 parliamentary elections that gave the party a 99 percent super majority.\\n\\nHe was also one of the closest allies to Mubarak's son, Gamal, and the two were viewed as the defining figures of the \\\"new guard\\\" within the party.\\n\\nThrough the policies committee of the party, of which the younger Mubarak was chairman and Ezz a member, the two steered the government into adopting aggressive neoliberal policies of free market capitalism, with the state selling off most of the companies nationalised in the 1960s by late President Gamal Abdel Nasser.\\n\\nDespite his advocacy for free market policies, Ezz, who was also a member of the lower house of parliament, the People's Assembly, has long been accused of holding a monopoly on the steel market.\"\n  }\n]"

On Salman's invitation, he hopped on board with Junoon\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"79619\",\n    \"score\": 0.4796041250228882,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Awaz - Wikipedia\\nauthor: Authority control databases Artists MusicBrainz\\ndate: 2006-08-24\\n---\\nname: Awaz\\nimage_size: 250\\nlandscape: yes\\norigin: Karachi, Sindh, Pakistan\\ngenre: Pop rock\\nyears_active: 1992\\u20132000\\nlabel: EMI Records, BMG Records, Lips Music Records\\nassociated_acts: The Barbarians, Karavan, Vital Signs, Junoon\\npast_members: Haroon RashidFaakhir MehmoodAsad Ahmed\\n\\nAwaz ( ) was a Pakistani pop band that formed in Islamabad in 1992. \\n\\nThe group was formed by Haroon Rashid, lead vocalist, who was soon joined by keyboardist Faakhir Mehmood and lead guitarist Asad Ahmed. In 2008, Pearlman was convicted and sentenced to 25 years in prison\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"29553\",\n    \"score\": 0.526704728603363,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Ezz sentenced to seven years and ordered to pay over EGP 19 billion\\ndate: 2012-10-04\\n---\\nAhmed Ezz, one of the most prominent figures in the former regime, has been convicted of money laundering and still faces charges of profiteering and illegally seizing public funds\\n\\nBy Ahmed Aboul Enein\\n\\nSteel tycoon, and former head of the National Democratic Party (NDP) organisation committee, Ahmed Ezz was sentenced to seven years in prison and ordered to pay over EGP 19 billion in fines by a Cairo criminal court on Thursday.\\n\\nEzz was found guilty of money laundering related to profiteering and illegally seizing public funds, charges for which he still faces trial.\\n\\nThe court found that Ezz laundered over EGP 6 billion. He was ordered to pay back the money, as well as additional damages of double that amount.\\n\\nHis trial over further charges of profiteering and illegally seizing public funds has been postponed until Tuesday 31 October.\\n\\nThe prosecution will accuse Ezz of making a deal with former Minister of Industry Ibrahim Mohamedeen. The former minister allegedly allowed Ezz to illegally take over the state-owned Dekheila steel company.\\n\\nEzz was a prominent figure in former President Hosni Mubarak's now defunct NDP. He was head of the organisation committee and was the architect of the 2010 parliamentary elections that gave the party a 99 percent super majority.\\n\\nHe was also one of the closest allies to Mubarak's son, Gamal, and the two were viewed as the defining figures of the \\\"new guard\\\" within the party.\\n\\nThrough the policies committee of the party, of which the younger Mubarak was chairman and Ezz a member, the two steered the government into adopting aggressive neoliberal policies of free market capitalism, with the state selling off most of the companies nationalised in the 1960s by late President Gamal Abdel Nasser.\\n\\nDespite his advocacy for free market policies, Ezz, who was also a member of the lower house of parliament, the People's Assembly, has long been accused of holding a monopoly on the steel market.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"19514\",\n    \"score\": 0.49803707003593445,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Full list of Trump's last-minute pardons and commuted sentences\\nauthor: Yuliya Talmazan; Rachel Elbaum; Sara Mhaidli\\ndate: 2021-01-20\\n---\\nWith only hours to go before leaving office, President Donald Trump pardoned 74 people and commuted the sentences of 70 others.\\n\\nA list of 143 people, made public early Wednesday morning, included his former chief strategist and longtime ally Steve Bannon as well as his former top fundraiser Elliott Broidy. Then, with less than an hour to go before President-elect Joe Biden was set to be sworn in, Trump granted one last pardon: to Albert J. Pirro, Jr., the ex-husband of Fox News host and longtime ally Jeanine Pirro.\\n\\nHere are some of the most notable names:\\n\\nAlex Adjmi: Adjmi was granted a full pardon. The White House said he was convicted in 1977 for a firearm violation and served one year's unsupervised probation.\\n\\nMichael Ashley: Ashley was convicted for bank fraud over the 2009 collapse of mortgage company Lend America and sentenced to 3 years in prison in 2019. He was taken into custody by U.S. Postal Inspection Service agents while on board the yacht of Chinese billionaire Guo Wengui. Bannon received a full pardon and now will not have to face a trial.\\n\\nLynn Barney: Trump granted a full pardon to Lynn Barney, who was sentenced to 35 months in prison for possessing a firearm as a previously convicted felon, after having previously been convicted for distributing a small amount of marijuana, according to the White House.\\n\\n\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"53237\",\n    \"score\": 0.49623650312423706,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Lee Jae Yong: who is the head of Samsung and why has he been jailed for bribery and embezzlement?\\nauthor: Matt Brooks this is a placeholder this is a placeholder this is a placeholder this is a placeholder\\ndate: 2021-01-18\\n---\\nLee Jae Yong: who is the head of Samsung and why has he been jailed for bribery and embezzlement?\\n\\nThis article contains affiliate links. We may earn a small commission on items purchased through this article, but that does not affect our editorial judgement.\\n\\nSamsung head Lee Jae Yong has been sentenced to two years and six months in prison for bribery.\\n\\nJae Yong and his father Lee Kun Hee have had a long association with the global tech company and were named the most powerful Koreans by Forbes Magazine in 2014, 35th on the worldwide list.\\n\\nAdvertisement\\n\\nHide AdAdvertisement\\n\\nHide AdSince then, Jae Yong has been de facto chairman of Samsung Electronics meaning the high court's ruling is likely to have widespread ramifications for the company and his position at it, at least immediately.\\n\\nBut who is Lee Jae Yong? Here's what you need to know.\\n\\nWho is Lee Jae Yong?\\n\\nHe was born in Seoul, in South Korea, on 23 June 1968 and is the son of Lee Kun Hee, who previously had two spells as chairman of the Samsung Group.\\n\\nKun Hee is widely credited with transforming the tech company into a worldwide conglomerate and leading manufacturer of smartphones, televisions and microchips.\\n\\nJae Yong's business acumen led to a Masters of Business Administration from Keio University - the oldest institution of modern higher education in Japan - and admittance to Harvard Business School.\\n\\nAdvertisement\\n\\nHide AdAdvertisement\\n\\nHide AdHe attended Harvard for five years in pursuit of a Doctor of Business Administration degree but did not graduate.\\n\\nA keen golfer, who also likes horseback riding, Jae Yong has one son and one daughter with his ex-wife Lim Se-ryung. He has two younger sisters, Lee Boo-jin and Lee Seo-hyun, while a third Lee Yoon-hyung died in 2005.\\n\\nHow did he become Samsung's top boss?\\n\\nHe joined Samsung in 1991 as vice president of strategic planning and then as chief customer officer but his prospects of future company leadership suffered a blow when his father was convicted of tax evasion.\\n\\nHis dad, who was pardoned, became chief operating officer of Samsung Electronics\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"52723\",\n    \"score\": 0.48104462027549744,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Samsung leader Jay Y. Lee given 5-year jail sentence for bribery\\nauthor: Joyce Lee\\ndate: 2017-08-25\\n---\\nSEOUL (Reuters) - The billionaire head of South Korea's Samsung Group, Jay Y. Lee, was sentenced to five years in jail for bribery on Friday in a watershed for the country's decades-long economic order dominated by powerful, family-run conglomerates.\\n\\nAfter a six-month trial over a scandal that brought down the then president, Park Geun-hye, a court ruled that Lee had paid bribes in anticipation of favours from Park.\\n\\nAdvertisement \\u00b7 Scroll to continue\\n\\nThe court also found Lee guilty of hiding assets abroad, embezzlement and perjury.\\n\\nLee, the 49-year-old heir to one of the world's biggest corporate empires, has been held since February on charges that he bribed Park to help secure control of a conglomerate that owns Samsung Electronics <005930.KS>, the world's leading smartphone and chip maker, and has interests ranging from drugs and home appliances to insurance and hotels.\\n\\nLee, who emerged stony-faced from the Seoul courtroom in a dark suit, but without a tie, and holding a document envelope, was escorted by justice ministry officials back to his detention centre.\\n\\nAdvertisement \\u00b7 Scroll to continue\\n\\n\\\"This case is a matter of Lee Jae-yong and Samsung Group executives, who had been steadily preparing for Lee's succession ... bribing the president,\\\" Seoul Central District Court Judge Kim Jin-dong said, using Lee's Korean name.\\n\\nKim said that as the group's heir apparent, Lee \\\"stood to benefit the most\\\" from any political favours for Samsung.\\n\\nLee denied wrongdoing, and one of his lawyers, Song Wu-cheol, said he would appeal.\\n\\n\\\"The entire guilty verdict is unacceptable,\\\" Song said, adding he was confident his client's innocence would be affirmed by a higher court. The case is expected to be appealed all the way up to the Supreme Court, likely next year.\\n\\nThe five year-sentence - one of the longest given to a South Korean business leader - is a landmark for South Korea, where the family-run conglomerates - or chaebols - have long been revered for helping transform the once war-ravaged country into a global economic powerhouse.\\n\\nBut they have more recently been criticized for holding back the economy and stifling small businesses and start-ups.\\n\\nSamsung, a symbol of the country's rise from poverty following the 1950-5\"\n  }\n]"

Ezz was enrolled in one of Egypt's leading international schools in the 1960s, and that had already guaranteed him an imbalanced playing field.\\n\\nThis would later on become a strong basis for the Egyptian public hating him \\u2013 or wishing they were him.\\n\\n\\\"With a curt wave of her hand, the wife of one of Egypt's richest men poses a question she already knows the answer to. Ezz was enrolled in one of Egypt's leading international schools in the 1960s, and that had already guaranteed him an imbalanced playing field.\\n\\nThis would later on become a strong basis for the Egyptian public hating him \\u2013 or wishing they were him.\\n\\n\\\"With a curt wave of her hand, the wife of one of Egypt's richest men poses a question she already knows the answer to. Yet, his father's close ties to late President Gamal Abdel Nasser garnered him a monthly 40-ton share in the country's steel to distribute. Quite a substantial amount at the time.\\n\\nYet The Washington Post reports that many of his defenders would argue that the tycoon was \\\"self-made\\\" even though evidence points to the contrary.\\n\\n\\\"Ezz's defenders say he deserved all the money he earned and came by it\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"56191\",\n    \"score\": 0.6285006999969482,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Egyptian billionaire Ahmed Ezz spends $11.1 million to boost stake in Ezz Steel\\nauthor: Omokolade Ajayi\\ndate: 2023-12-22\\n---\\nTable of Contents\\n\\nEgyptian billionaire businessman Ahmed Ezz, founder of leading steelmaker Ezz Steel, has further solidified his control over the company by snapping up additional shares in a deal worth EGP344 million ($11.1 million).\\n\\nThe transaction, brokered by Hermes Financial Group, saw Ezz acquire roughly 4.3 million shares at an average price of EGP80 ($2.59) per share from fellow Egyptian steel magnate Jamal El-Garhy \\u2014 this strengthens Ezz's position as the majority shareholder.\\n\\nLatest purchase strengthens Ezz's grip\\n\\nEzz Steel \\u2014 the largest independent steel producer in the Middle East and North Africa \\u2014 has delivered impressive financial results in recent times, further strengthening investors' interest and confidence. With a total output of 5.14 million metric tonnes, Ezz Steel is far ahead of Saudi Arabia's Hadeed and Emirates Steel.\\n\\nPrior to the transaction, Ezz held a commanding 60.71-percent stake. Mineral Investment Development and El-Garhy Steel Group followed with 7.44 percent and 5.93 percent, respectively. The latest purchase strengthens Ezz's grip, solidifying his position as the group's dominant shareholder.\\n\\nEzz Steel dominates MENA market with stellar financial performance\\n\\nEzz Steel's financial performance in the first nine months of 2023 has been nothing short of impressive. Profits soared to EGP27.9 billion ($883.1 million), a significant jump from the previous year's EGP22.1 billion ($709.6 million). Sales followed suit, surging from EGP60.6 billion ($1.96 billion) to EGP103.2 billion ($3.34 billion) \\u2013 a 70-percent increase year-over-year.\\n\\nEzz's latest acquisition comes on the heels of a significant surge in Ezz Steel's share price on the Egyptian Exchange. Between Nov. 1 and 22, the market value of his existing stake climbed by EGP1.77 billion ($57.53 million), solidifying his position as both a leading investor on the bourse and one of the country's wealthiest individuals.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"86230\",\n    \"score\": 0.6260731816291809,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Ahmed Ezz takes direct controlling stake in Ezz Steel\\ndate: 2021-06-08\\n---\\n\\nAhmed Ezz now directly owns a controlling stake in Ezz Steel after purchasing a 33.4% stake in the company from El Ezz Group Holding for Industry and Investment, according to an EGX disclosure (pdf). He was ordered to pay back the money, as well as additional damages of double that amount.\\n\\nHis trial over further charges of profiteering and illegally seizing public funds has been postponed until Tuesday 31 October.\\n\\nThe prosecution will accuse Ezz of making a deal with former Minister of Industry Ibrahim Mohamedeen. The former minister allegedly allowed Ezz to illegally take over the state-owned Dekheila steel company.\\n\\nEzz was a prominent figure in former President Hosni Mubarak's now defunct NDP. He was head of the organisation committee and was the architect of the 2010 parliamentary elections that gave the party a 99 percent super majority.\\n\\nHe was also one of the closest allies to Mubarak's son, Gamal, and the two were viewed as the defining figures of the \\\"new guard\\\" within the party.\\n\\nThrough the policies committee of the party, of which the younger Mubarak was chairman and Ezz a member, the two steered the government into adopting aggressive neoliberal policies of free market capitalism, with the state selling off most of the companies nationalised in the 1960s by late President Gamal Abdel Nasser.\\n\\nDespite his advocacy for free market policies, Ezz, who was also a member of the lower house of parliament, the People's Assembly, has long been accused of holding a monopoly on the steel market.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"72355\",\n    \"score\": 0.588110089302063,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Ahmed Ezz - Wikipedia\\ndate: 2016-02-13\\n---\\nAhmed Ezz may refer to:\\n\\n* Ahmed Ezz (actor) (born 1971), Egyptian actor\\n* Ahmed Ezz (businessman) (born 1959), Egyptian businessman and politician\"\n  }\n]"

This essay explores the knotty question of when legal corporate action is corrupt. It argues that when corporations exercise public power, either through monopolistic control of a market or through campaign contributions and support of governmental actors, they are subject to the same responsibilities of anyone who exercises public power. Therefore, as a theoretical matter, we should call corporations corrupt when they exercise public power selfishly, in a way that puts their own interests over the public's interests. Because they make legal corporate corruption less likely, global anticorruption campaigns should therefore emphasize antimonopoly laws and campaign finance laws.\\n\\nShould we call legal corporate political behavior corrupt? If so, when?\\n\\nIt is a tricky issue. Of course, in some cases, corporate actors engage in illegal bribes of public officials, and we can easily label this behavior corrupt.1 But more frequently, corporate actors use sophisticated legal means to exercise power over public officials: by making campaign contributions, lobbying, exerting media influence, funding nonprofits, sponsoring think tanks, paying speaking fees, or even cornering the market on key goods and services, creating public dependencies on the corporation. These kinds of behaviors make up what Michael Johnston has termed \\\"influence markets,\\\" which he identifies as the primary mode of corruption in developed democracies.2 These behaviors are also explored in depth in the works of sociologist Amitai Etzioni.3 All of these behaviors are not only legal in the United States, but are encouraged and taught as essential strategies in business schools. They also have the tendency to spread. Having built their power within the United States or similar legal systems, corporations then use legal tools to exert influence in other countries. Depending on which side of the law they stand on, corporate actors may push to legalize the most powerful of their mechanisms of control, criminalizing the tools used by weaker societal agents, or they may exercise their influence to decriminalize their behaviors in a new market. Nathan Deal and the Longest Corruption Scandal in Georgia History\\ndate: 2014-10-22\\n---\\nBack in 2007, Georgia Revenue Commissioner Bart Graham noticed something funny in the state budget. What he discovered would bring to light a scandal then nearly 20 years old, yet which still hasn't ended.\\n\\nWhat caught Graham's attention was a scheme set up in 1990 that granted regional monopolies to a handful of businesses for performing mandatory title inspections on salvaged cars. Funny thing, not only did these shops have no competition, but they never bid for the contracts, and on top of that, the state was paying the inspectors to the tune of well over a million dollars a year.\\n\\nAnd lo and behold, the sweetest contract\\u2014for the populous region, including Gainesville and Atlanta, where fees were higher than anywhere else\\u2014had been handed to a company called Gainesville Salvage Disposal, co-owned by none other than Nathan Deal, a state senator in 1990, and, by 2007, a U.S. representative in Washington. With a total output of 5.14 million metric tonnes, Ezz Steel is far ahead of Saudi Arabia's Hadeed and Emirates Steel.\\n\\nPrior to the transaction, Ezz held a commanding 60.71-percent stake. Mineral Investment Development and El-Garhy Steel Group followed with 7.44 percent and 5.93 percent, respectively. The latest purchase strengthens Ezz's grip, solidifying his position as the group's dominant shareholder.\\n\\nEzz Steel dominates MENA market with stellar financial performance\\n\\nEzz Steel's financial performance in the first nine months of 2023 has been nothing short of impressive. Profits soared to EGP27.9 billion ($883.1 million), a significant jump from the previous year's EGP22.1 billion ($709.6 million). Sales followed suit, surging from EGP60.6 billion ($1.96 billion) to EGP103.2 billion ($3.34 billion) \\u2013 a 70-percent increase year-over-year.\\n\\nEzz's latest acquisition comes on the heels of a significant surge in Ezz Steel's share price on the Egyptian Exchange. Between Nov. 1 and 22, the market value of his existing stake climbed by EGP1.77 billion ($57.53 million), solidifying his position as both a leading investor on the bourse and one of the country's wealthiest individuals.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"86230\",\n    \"score\": 0.5517640113830566,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Ahmed Ezz takes direct controlling stake in Ezz Steel\\ndate: 2021-06-08\\n---\\n\\nAhmed Ezz now directly owns a controlling stake in Ezz Steel after purchasing a 33.4% stake in the company from El Ezz Group Holding for Industry and Investment, according to an EGX disclosure (pdf). The steel magnate, who owns almost 100% of Ezz Holding, now directly holds a 65.7% stake in Ezz Steel after purchasing almost 182 mn global depository receipts from the affiliated company. This comes less than a month after Ezz purchased a 5.6% stake in Ezz Steel, again from Ezz Holding.\\n\\n\\nEnterprise is a daily publication of Enterprise Ventures LLC, an Egyptian limited liability company (commercial register 83594), and a subsidiary of Inktank Communications. He has been a member of various musical groups and some of the earliest Pakistani rock bands like The Barbarians, Awaz, Karavan, Junoon, Vital Signs and Coke Studio Pakistan.\\n\\nEarly life\\n\\nHis family moved to Dubai when he was quite young. His elder brother was a guitarist and when he left for college, he left his guitar back at home. Asad picked it up and quickly learned to play. His family returned to Karachi in 1984.\\n\\nPersonal life\\n\\nOn 14 February 2019, Ahmed married Hira after dating her for two years. They got married in a nikah ceremony surrounded by close family and friends in Karachi.\\n\\nCareer\\n\\nCoke Studio (Pakistan)\\n\\nAsad played in Coke Studio (Produced by Rohail Hyatt) and was one of the house band members from season 2 (2008) to season 6 (2012) and reappeared in Season 13 in 2020. His style of guitar playing has some flashy showmanship in it.\\n\\nThe Barbarians\\n\\nAsad started his music career in 1987 with The Barbarians, which is regarded by many as Pakistan's first rock band. The band's first single \\\"Yeh Zindagi Hai\\\" (This is Life) set the foundation of Pakistani rock. \\n\\nThey released their only album, the self-titled \\\"The Barbarians\\\" in 1989 with the label EMI (Pakistan), which did not fare well in the then rock-repellant Pakistani music industry. The Barbarians band fell apart in 1990.\\n\\nJunoon and Vital Signs\\n\\nAsad did a gig with Salman Ahmad of Junoon at a party in 1991. On Salman's invitation, he hopped on board with Junoon\"\n  }\n]"

        "content": "[\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"72355\",\n    \"score\": 0.6709632277488708,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Ahmed Ezz - Wikipedia\\ndate: 2016-02-13\\n---\\nAhmed Ezz may refer to:\\n\\n* Ahmed Ezz (actor) (born 1971), Egyptian actor\\n* Ahmed Ezz (businessman) (born 1959), Egyptian businessman and politician\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"47857\",\n    \"score\": 0.6329580545425415,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Profile: Who is steel tycoon Ahmed Ezz?\\ndate: 2018-03-03\\n---\\nCAIRO \\u2013 3 March 2018: Having reconciled with the Egyptian state after seven years of lawsuits, steel tycoon and politician Ahmed Ezz, known for his Mubarak-era corruption and embezzlement cases, is our spotlight guest.\\n\\nEzz was born to an Egyptian father, Lieutant Abdel Aziz Ezz, and a Palestinian mother, Afaf Halawa, in 1959; into a family that had \\\"traded building materials for generations,\\\" according to The Washington Post. Later on, when Ezz would become a political and economic tycoon in Egyptian society, his opposition would manipulate his background to claim that his mother was Jewish, which should disallow him from joining and playing in Egyptian politics, Sky News Arabia stated.\\n\\nThe tycoon had taken to walking with an air of superiority from a young age; he gained a strong sense of self-esteem when he began excelling at school, Sky News Arabia explained. Ezz was enrolled in one of Egypt's leading international schools in the 1960s, and that had already guaranteed him an imbalanced playing field.\\n\\nThis would later on become a strong basis for the Egyptian public hating him \\u2013 or wishing they were him.\\n\\n\\\"With a curt wave of her hand, the wife of one of Egypt's richest men poses a question she already knows the answer to. 'Who is sympathetic to the billionaire?' Abla Ezz asks. 'No one,'\\\" The Washington Post wrote in 2011.\\n\\nBut from an early age, Ezz took a strong interest in his father's business. He would supervise their outlet in the local area of Al Sabteya.\\n\\nHis father left the Egyptian army after the 1967 Naksa; at the time when the Egyptian government were carrying out a purging campaign on the army. At\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"79619\",\n    \"score\": 0.4753503203392029,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Awaz - Wikipedia\\nauthor: Authority control databases Artists MusicBrainz\\ndate: 2006-08-24\\n---\\nname: Awaz\\nimage_size: 250\\nlandscape: yes\\norigin: Karachi, Sindh, Pakistan\\ngenre: Pop rock\\nyears_active: 1992\\u20132000\\nlabel: EMI Records, BMG Records, Lips Music Records\\nassociated_acts: The Barbarians, Karavan, Vital Signs, Junoon\\npast_members: Haroon RashidFaakhir MehmoodAsad Ahmed\\n\\nAwaz ( ) was a Pakistani pop band that formed in Islamabad in 1992. \\n\\nThe group was formed by Haroon Rashid, lead vocalist, who was soon joined by keyboardist Faakhir Mehmood and lead guitarist Asad Ahmed. Awaz were one of the pioneer bands of the local pop music scene and were highly skilled and talented musicians, producers and composers. The band's skill at composing and producing was often overlooked and the focus was on their good looks, glossy videos, catchy songs and wild stage performances.Haroon Biography Retrieved on 27 December 2010\\n\\nAwaz achieved commercial success in Pakistan with the release of their self-titled debut album, Awaz, in 1993. The single \\\"Janeman\\\" was an instant hit as they became the first band from South Asia to appear on MTV in April 1992, composed by lead vocalist Haroon Rashid, produced by Haroon and Faakhir with lyrics written by Sarmed Mirza and Haroon. Their second studio album, Jadoo Ka Charagh, was released in 1995, and included the hit singles \\\"Jadoo Ka Charagh\\\" and \\\"Shawa\\\". The album proved to be better than the first studio release and stood up to everybody's expectations. In 1996, the band went on to record and release their third studio album, Shola, which included their biggest hit song \\\"Mr. Fraudiay\\\". Their third album comprised elements of western music and less traditional eastern music unlike the previous albums had. The very patriotic number Ay Jawaan was one of their most loved songs, followed by Jadoo Ka Chiragh and the comic, Mr Fraudiye. Due to a dispute between the members in late 1999, Haroon and Faakhir went on to pursue their solo careers while Asad Ahmed formed\"\n  }\n]"

Ezz was enrolled in one of Egypt's leading international schools in the 1960s, and that had already guaranteed him an imbalanced playing field.\\n\\nThis would later on become a strong basis for the Egyptian public hating him \\u2013 or wishing they were him.\\n\\n\\\"With a curt wave of her hand, the wife of one of Egypt's richest men poses a question she already knows the answer to. 'Who is sympathetic to the billionaire?' Abla Ezz asks. 'No one,'\\\" The Washington Post wrote in 2011.\\n\\nBut from an early age, Ezz took a strong interest in his father's business. He would supervise their outlet in the local area of Al Sabteya.\\n\\nHis father left the Egyptian army after the 1967 Naksa; at the time when the Egyptian government were carrying out a purging campaign on the army. Even though he wasn't liable for losing the war, Ezz's father was still barred, Sky News Arabia mentioned. Yet, his father's close ties to late President Gamal Abdel Nasser garnered him a monthly 40-ton share in the country's steel to distribute. Quite a substantial amount at the time.\\n\\nYet The Washington Post reports that many of his defenders would argue that the tycoon was \\\"self-made\\\" even though evidence points to the contrary.\\n\\n\\\"Ezz's defenders say he deserved all the money he earned and came by it\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"90680\",\n    \"score\": 0.5301591753959656,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Asad Ahmed - Wikipedia\\ndate: 2007-10-02\\n---\\nname: Asad Ahmed\\nnative_name: \\u0627\\u0633\\u062f \\u0627\\u062d\\u0645\\u062f\\nnative_name_lang: ur\\nbirth_date: 21 July 1971\\nbirth_place: Karachi, Pakistan\\norigin: Karachi, Pakistan\\noccupation: Musician, Songwriter, Record producer, Entrepreneur\\ngenre: Hard rock, heavy metal\\ninstrument: Guitar\\ncurrent_member_of: KaravanAwazVital Signs\\nyears_active: 1987 \\u2013 present\\n\\nAsad Ahmed (born 21 July 1971) is a Pakistani guitarist. He has been a member of various musical groups and some of the earliest Pakistani rock bands like The Barbarians, Awaz, Karavan, Junoon, Vital Signs and Coke Studio Pakistan.\\n\\nEarly life\\n\\nHis family moved to Dubai when he was quite young. His elder brother was a guitarist and when he left for college, he left his guitar back at home. Asad picked it up and quickly learned to play. His family returned to Karachi in 1984.\\n\\nPersonal life\\n\\nOn 14 February 2019, Ahmed married Hira after dating her for two years. They got married in a nikah ceremony surrounded by close family and friends in Karachi.\\n\\nCareer\\n\\nCoke Studio (Pakistan)\\n\\nAsad played in Coke Studio (Produced by Rohail Hyatt) and was one of the house band members from season 2 (2008) to season 6 (2012) and reappeared in Season 13 in 2020. His style of guitar playing has some flashy showmanship in it.\\n\\nThe Barbarians\\n\\nAsad started his music career in 1987 with The Barbarians, which is regarded by many as Pakistan's first rock band. The band's first single \\\"Yeh Zindagi Hai\\\" (This is Life) set the foundation of Pakistani rock. \\n\\nThey released their only album, the self-titled \\\"The Barbarians\\\" in 1989 with the label EMI (Pakistan), which did not fare well in the then rock-repellant Pakistani music industry. The Barbarians band fell apart in 1990.\\n\\nJunoon and Vital Signs\\n\\nAsad did a gig with Salman Ahmad of Junoon at a party in 1991. On Salman's invitation, he hopped on board with Junoon\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"31823\",\n    \"score\": 0.5258333086967468,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Abdel Halim Hafez - Wikipedia\\nauthor: Authority control databases\\ndate: 2005-10-03\\n---\\nname: Abdel Halim Hafez\\u0639\\u0628\\u062f \\u0627\\u0644\\u062d\\u0644\\u064a\\u0645 \\u062d\\u0627\\u0641\\u0638\\nhonorific_prefix: ORE\\nbirth_name: Abdel Halim Ali Shabana\\u0639\\u0628\\u062f \\u0627\\u0644\\u062d\\u0644\\u064a\\u0645 \\u0639\\u0644\\u064a \\u0634\\u0628\\u0627\\u0646\\u0629\\nbirth_date: 21 June 1929\\nbirth_place: El-Halawat, El Sharqia, Kingdom of Egypt\\ndeath_date: 30 03 1977\\ndeath_place: London, England\\ngenre: Egyptian music, Classical Arabic Music\\noccupations: Singer, actor, music teacher, conductor, film producer\\nyears_active: 1952\\u20131977\\nlabel: Mazzika\\n\\nAbdel Halim Ali Shabana (), commonly known as Abdel Halim Hafez (, ) (21 June 1929 \\u2013 30 March 1977), was an Egyptian singer, actor, conductor, businessman, music teacher and film producer.\\n\\nAbdel Halim is considered to be one of the greatest Egyptian musicians of his era, along with Umm Kulthum, Mohamed Abdel Wahab, Farid Al Atrach, Mohamed Fawzi, and Shadia. As his popularity grew, he was given the nickname 'el-Andaleeb el-Asmar (), meaning The Dark-Skinned Nightingale. He achieved extraordinary success as a popular musician throughout the Arab world, with estimated sales of over 80 million records.\\n\\nEarly life\\n\\nBorn Abdel Halim Ali Shabanah in El-Halawat in El Sharqia, 80 kilometers (50 miles) north of Cairo, he was the fourth child of Ali Ismail Shabanah. He had two brothers, Ismail and Mohamed, and one sister, Alyah. His mother died from labor complications three days after giving birth to him \\u2013 something that made people around him believe that he brought bad luck. His father died as well a few months later, leaving him and his siblings orphaned at a young age. He lived in a poor orphanage for a number of years. He was later raised by his aunt and uncle in Cairo. During these years Abdel Halim was extremely poor.\\n\\nAbdel Halim's musical abilities first became apparent while he was in primary school and his older brother Ismail Shabanah was his first music teacher. At\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"50495\",\n    \"score\": 0.5219799876213074,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: The 50 Best Arabic Pop Songs of the 21st Century\\ndate: 2024-04-10\\n---\\n\\\\n\\\\t<\\\\/div>\\\\n<\\\\/div>\\\\n\\\\t\\\\t\\\\t<\\\\/div>\\\\n\\\\t\\\\t\\\\t\\\\t<\\\\/div>\\\\n\\\",\\\"data\\\":[{\\\"divId\\\":\\\"gpt-dsk-tab-list-inbody1-uid0\\\",\\\"displayType\\\":\\\"banner\\\",\\\"targeting\\\":[{\\\"key\\\":\\\"pos\\\",\\\"value\\\":\\\"in-list1\\\"},{\\\"key\\\":\\\"pos\\\",\\\"value\\\":\\\"mid\\\"},{\\\"key\\\":\\\"pos\\\",\\\"value\\\":\\\"btf\\\"},{\\\"key\\\":\\\"pos\\\",\\\"value\\\":\\\"inbody1\\\"}],\\\"lazyLoad\\\":\\\"no\\\",\\\"lazyLoadMultiplier\\\":2,\\\"zone\\\":\\\"music\\\\/list\\\\/inbody1\\\",\\\"sizes\\\":[[728,90],[6,6]]}]}},{\\\"ID\\\":1235002045,\\\"position\\\":1,\\\"positionDisplay\\\":49,\\\"date\\\":\\\"2024-04-10 16:25:28\\\",\\\"modified\\\":\\\"2024-04-24 17:59:30\\\",\\\"title\\\":\\\"Ahmed Saad, 'El Youm El Helw Dah'\\\",\\\"subtitle\\\":null,\\\"slug\\\":\\\"ahmed-saad-el-youm-el-helw-dah-1235002045\\\",\\\"caption\\\":\\\"\\\",\\\"description\\\":\\\"\\\\n\\\\t\\\\t\\\\t\\\\t\\n\\n\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n\\n\\n\\\\n\\\\tThe chart-topping Egyptian singer and actor Ahmed Saad released this song for the film Ahmum, <\\\\/em>a comedy about three cousins who inherit a fortune from their uncle. The ubiquitous hit is a feel-good track about having a good time on a beautiful day with the people you love. Saad has been on a roll in recent years, with major songs like \\\"Ekhtayaraty\\\" and \\\"El Melouk,\\\" the latter a collaboration with fellow Egyptian artists 3enba and Double Zuksh that was featured in the Disney+ series Moon Knight<\\\\/em>.<\\\\/p>\\\\n<\\\\/div>\\\",\\\"alt\\\":\\\"Ahmed Saad is singing at the opening of the Egypt Capital Cup tournament at the FIFA Series between Egypt and New Zealand at New Capital Stadium in Egypt, on March 22, 2024. (Photo by Ayman Aref\\\\/NurPhoto via Getty Images)\\\",\\\"image_credit\\\":\\\"Ayman Aref\\\\/NurPhoto\\\\/Getty Images\"\n  }\n]"

Quite a substantial amount at the time.\\n\\nYet The Washington Post reports that many of his defenders would argue that the tycoon was \\\"self-made\\\" even though evidence points to the contrary.\\n\\n\\\"Ezz's defenders say he deserved all the money he earned and came by it\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"79619\",\n    \"score\": 0.46172699332237244,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Awaz - Wikipedia\\nauthor: Authority control databases Artists MusicBrainz\\ndate: 2006-08-24\\n---\\nname: Awaz\\nimage_size: 250\\nlandscape: yes\\norigin: Karachi, Sindh, Pakistan\\ngenre: Pop rock\\nyears_active: 1992\\u20132000\\nlabel: EMI Records, BMG Records, Lips Music Records\\nassociated_acts: The Barbarians, Karavan, Vital Signs, Junoon\\npast_members: Haroon RashidFaakhir MehmoodAsad Ahmed\\n\\nAwaz ( ) was a Pakistani pop band that formed in Islamabad in 1992. \\n\\nThe group was formed by Haroon Rashid, lead vocalist, who was soon joined by keyboardist Faakhir Mehmood and lead guitarist Asad Ahmed. Awaz were one of the pioneer bands of the local pop music scene and were highly skilled and talented musicians, producers and composers. The band's skill at composing and producing was often overlooked and the focus was on their good looks, glossy videos, catchy songs and wild stage performances.Haroon Biography Retrieved on 27 December 2010\\n\\nAwaz achieved commercial success in Pakistan with the release of their self-titled debut album, Awaz, in 1993. The single \\\"Janeman\\\" was an instant hit as they became the first band from South Asia to appear on MTV in April 1992, composed by lead vocalist Haroon Rashid, produced by Haroon and Faakhir with lyrics written by Sarmed Mirza and Haroon. Their second studio album, Jadoo Ka Charagh, was released in 1995, and included the hit singles \\\"Jadoo Ka Charagh\\\" and \\\"Shawa\\\". The album proved to be better than the first studio release and stood up to everybody's expectations. In 1996, the band went on to record and release their third studio album, Shola, which included their biggest hit song \\\"Mr. Fraudiay\\\". Their third album comprised elements of western music and less traditional eastern music unlike the previous albums had. Later on, when Ezz would become a political and economic tycoon in Egyptian society, his opposition would manipulate his background to claim that his mother was Jewish, which should disallow him from joining and playing in Egyptian politics, Sky News Arabia stated.\\n\\nThe tycoon had taken to walking with an air of superiority from a young age; he gained a strong sense of self-esteem when he began excelling at school, Sky News Arabia explained. Ezz was enrolled in one of Egypt's leading international schools in the 1960s, and that had already guaranteed him an imbalanced playing field.\\n\\nThis would later on become a strong basis for the Egyptian public hating him \\u2013 or wishing they were him.\\n\\n\\\"With a curt wave of her hand, the wife of one of Egypt's richest men poses a question she already knows the answer to. Quite a substantial amount at the time.\\n\\nYet The Washington Post reports that many of his defenders would argue that the tycoon was \\\"self-made\\\" even though evidence points to the contrary.\\n\\n\\\"Ezz's defenders say he deserved all the money he earned and came by it\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"15579\",\n    \"score\": 0.5176665782928467,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Adel Emam - Wikipedia\\nauthor: Authority control databases\\ndate: 2004-12-29\\n---\\nname: Adel Emam\\nbirth_name: Adel Mohammed Emam Mohammed Bukhariny\\nnative_name: \\u0639\\u0627\\u062f\\u0644 \\u0625\\u0645\\u0627\\u0645\\nbirth_date: 17 05 1940\\nbirth_place: Mansoura, Kingdom of Egypt\\nnationality: Egyptian\\nnickname: El Zaeem (The Leader)\\noccupation: Actor, comedian\\nyears_active: 1962\\u20132024\\nspouse: Hala Al Shalaqani\\nchildren: 3, including Mohamed Emam and Ramy Imam\\ncitizenship: Egypt\\neducation: Cairo University\\nrelatives: Mustafa Metwalli (brother-in-law)\\n\\nAdel Mohammed Emam (; born on 17 May 1940), is an Egyptian film, television, and stage actor, known for his extensive career with over 150 artistic works, including films, plays, and television series spanning comedy, social, and political genres. He is regarded as one of the leading figures of the second generation of comedy artists in Egypt and the Arab world. He is primarily a comedian, but he has starred in more serious works and, combined comedy with romance especially in his earlier secondary roles in films such as My Wife, the Director General, My Wife's Dignity, My Wife's Goblin and Virgo, all films starring Salah Zulfikar. \\n\\nEmam stands as a towering figure in Egyptian and Arab cinema, celebrated for his versatility across genres. Starting in the 1960s, he became one of the most well-known figures in the industry. Emam earned a bachelor's degree in Agriculture from Cairo University. Since then he has appeared in over 103 movies and 10 plays. Emam's personal life is connected to the world of arts. With a total output of 5.14 million metric tonnes, Ezz Steel is far ahead of Saudi Arabia's Hadeed and Emirates Steel.\\n\\nPrior to the transaction, Ezz held a commanding 60.71-percent stake. Here's who they are\\ndate: 2025-06-07\\n---\\nTrump has tapped an unprecedented 13 billionaires for his administration. Here's who they are\\n\\nThe nominees make up the richest presidential administration in modern history.\\n\\nPresident-elect Donald Trump has assembled the wealthiest presidential administration in modern history, with at least 13 billionaires set to take on government posts.\\n\\nThey include a wrestling magnate, a private space pioneer, a New York real estate developer, the heir to a small appliance empire, and the wealthiest man on the planet -- with several being donors and close personal friends of the incoming president.\\n\\nIn total, the combined net worth of the wealthiest members of his administration could surpass $460 billion, including Department of Government Efficiency co-head Elon Musk -- whose net worth of more than $400 billion exceeds the GDP of mid-sized countries.\\n\\nEven discounting Musk, Trump's cabinet is still expected to be the wealthiest in history, with reported billionaires Howard Lutnick nominated as commerce secretary, Linda McMahon nominated as education secretary, and Scott Bessent nominated as treasury secretary. In contrast, the wealthiest official in the Biden administration is White House Chief of Staff Jeff Zients, whose disclosures from 2021 showed his net worth\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"24475\",\n    \"score\": 0.4868025481700897,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: 18 Famous Musicians Who Went from Rich to Bankrupt\\ndate: 1996-01-01\\n---\\nNot all broke musicians remain broke, but the road to recovery is harder than the fall to financial ruin. It's not uncommon for an artist to rise to stardom fast, and with that fast rise to fame comes quick fortune. Many people who did not grow up with wealth are not prepared or educated on how to handle money. Others are swept up by stardom and wrecklessly spend their money thinking their stardom, and income will never go away (the broke rock star trope). Some artists simply get caught in expensive drug habits that alter both their bank size and their better judgement. Finally, other poorer souls are swindled by the very people they trusted most such as their families or managers. These 18 famous musicians lost it all one way or another. Some of these musicians recovered, while sadly, some died poor.\\n\\n#\\n\\n1\\n\\nMeat Loaf (Marvin Lee Aday) sold records. A lot of records. \\\"Bat Out of Hell\\\" sold approximately 43 million copies. So how did a dude who sold so many records go broke?\\n\\nAfter finding success with \\\"Bat Out Of Hell\\\" he naturally decided to record a follow-up. But there was a little problem. He had lost his voice. At around the same time, his old producer Jim Steinman, along with others had decided to sue Meat Loaf. With over 40 lawsuits mounted against Marvin - his only recourse was filing chapter 11 bankruptcy.\\n\\nLuckily, for Meat Loaf, he found success once more in 1993 with \\\"Bat Out Of Hell II: Back Into Hell\\\" which featured the famous song which still has people asking \\\"won't do what?!\\\"\\n\\n#\\n\\n2\\n\\nToni Braxton has sold over 67 million records and has won seven Grammys. Here's another number - 2. That's how many times she's declared bankruptcy.\\n\\nShe first declared bankruptcy in 1998 from credit card bills and exorbitant monthly expenses. Luckily, two years later in 2000, she jump-started her career with her new album \\\"The Heat.\\\"\\n\\nBut, financial woes struck again. He was later raised by his aunt and uncle in Cairo. During these years Abdel Halim was extremely poor.\\n\\nAbdel Halim's musical abilities first became apparent while he was in primary school and his older brother Ismail Shabanah was his first music teacher. Later on, when Ezz would become a political and economic tycoon in Egyptian society, his opposition would manipulate his background to claim that his mother was Jewish, which should disallow him from joining and playing in Egyptian politics, Sky News Arabia stated.\\n\\nThe tycoon had taken to walking with an air of superiority from a young age; he gained a strong sense of self-esteem when he began excelling at school, Sky News Arabia explained. Ezz was enrolled in one of Egypt's leading international schools in the 1960s, and that had already guaranteed him an imbalanced playing field.\\n\\nThis would later on become a strong basis for the Egyptian public hating him \\u2013 or wishing they were him.\\n\\n\\\"With a curt wave of her hand, the wife of one of Egypt's richest men poses a question she already knows the answer to. Yet, his father's close ties to late President Gamal Abdel Nasser garnered him a monthly 40-ton share in the country's steel to distribute. With a total output of 5.14 million metric tonnes, Ezz Steel is far ahead of Saudi Arabia's Hadeed and Emirates Steel.\\n\\nPrior to the transaction, Ezz held a commanding 60.71-percent stake. Mineral Investment Development and El-Garhy Steel Group followed with 7.44 percent and 5.93 percent, respectively. The latest purchase strengthens Ezz's grip, solidifying his position as the group's dominant shareholder.\\n\\nEzz Steel dominates MENA market with stellar financial performance\\n\\nEzz Steel's financial performance in the first nine months of 2023 has been nothing short of impressive. Between Nov. 1 and 22, the market value of his existing stake climbed by EGP1.77 billion ($57.53 million), solidifying his position as both a leading investor on the bourse and one of the country's wealthiest individuals.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"29553\",\n    \"score\": 0.6333562731742859,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Ezz sentenced to seven years and ordered to pay over EGP 19 billion\\ndate: 2012-10-04\\n---\\nAhmed Ezz, one of the most prominent figures in the former regime, has been convicted of money laundering and still faces charges of profiteering and illegally seizing public funds\\n\\nBy Ahmed Aboul Enein\\n\\nSteel tycoon, and former head of the National Democratic Party (NDP) organisation committee, Ahmed Ezz was sentenced to seven years in prison and ordered to pay over EGP 19 billion in fines by a Cairo criminal court on Thursday.\\n\\nEzz was found guilty of money laundering related to profiteering and illegally seizing public funds, charges for which he still faces trial.\\n\\nThe court found that Ezz laundered over EGP 6 billion. He was ordered to pay back the money, as well as additional damages of double that amount.\\n\\nHis trial over further charges of profiteering and illegally seizing public funds has been postponed until Tuesday 31 October.\\n\\nThe prosecution will accuse Ezz of making a deal with former Minister of Industry Ibrahim Mohamedeen. The former minister allegedly allowed Ezz to illegally take over the state-owned Dekheila steel company.\\n\\nEzz was a prominent figure in former President Hosni Mubarak's now defunct NDP. He has been a member of various musical groups and some of the earliest Pakistani rock bands like The Barbarians, Awaz, Karavan, Junoon, Vital Signs and Coke Studio Pakistan.\\n\\nEarly life\\n\\nHis family moved to Dubai when he was quite young. His elder brother was a guitarist and when he left for college, he left his guitar back at home. Asad picked it up and quickly learned to play. His family returned to Karachi in 1984.\\n\\nPersonal life\\n\\nOn 14 February 2019, Ahmed married Hira after dating her for two years. They got married in a nikah ceremony surrounded by close family and friends in Karachi.\\n\\nCareer\\n\\nCoke Studio (Pakistan)\\n\\nAsad played in Coke Studio (Produced by Rohail Hyatt) and was one of the house band members from season 2 (2008) to season 6 (2012) and reappeared in Season 13 in 2020.         "content": "[\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"47857\",\n    \"score\": 0.6338643431663513,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Profile: Who is steel tycoon Ahmed Ezz?\\ndate: 2018-03-03\\n---\\nCAIRO \\u2013 3 March 2018: Having reconciled with the Egyptian state after seven years of lawsuits, steel tycoon and politician Ahmed Ezz, known for his Mubarak-era corruption and embezzlement cases, is our spotlight guest.\\n\\nEzz was born to an Egyptian father, Lieutant Abdel Aziz Ezz, and a Palestinian mother, Afaf Halawa, in 1959; into a family that had \\\"traded building materials for generations,\\\" according to The Washington Post. Later on, when Ezz would become a political and economic tycoon in Egyptian society, his opposition would manipulate his background to claim that his mother was Jewish, which should disallow him from joining and playing in Egyptian politics, Sky News Arabia stated.\\n\\nThe tycoon had taken to walking with an air of superiority from a young age; he gained a strong sense of self-esteem when he began excelling at school, Sky News Arabia explained. Ezz was enrolled in one of Egypt's leading international schools in the 1960s, and that had already guaranteed him an imbalanced playing field.\\n\\nThis would later on become a strong basis for the Egyptian public hating him \\u2013 or wishing they were him.\\n\\n\\\"With a curt wave of her hand, the wife of one of Egypt's richest men poses a question she already knows the answer to. 'Who is sympathetic to the billionaire?' Abla Ezz asks. 'No one,'\\\" The Washington Post wrote in 2011.\\n\\nBut from an early age, Ezz took a strong interest in his father's business. With a total output of 5.14 million metric tonnes, Ezz Steel is far ahead of Saudi Arabia's Hadeed and Emirates Steel.\\n\\nPrior to the transaction, Ezz held a commanding 60.71-percent stake. Mineral Investment Development and El-Garhy Steel Group followed with 7.44 percent and 5.93 percent, respectively. The latest purchase strengthens Ezz's grip, solidifying his position as the group's dominant shareholder.\\n\\nEzz Steel dominates MENA market with stellar financial performance\\n\\nEzz Steel's financial performance in the first nine months of 2023 has been nothing short of impressive. Profits soared to EGP27.9 billion ($883.1 million), a significant jump from the previous year's EGP22.1 billion ($709.6 million). Sales followed suit, surging from EGP60.6 billion ($1.96 billion) to EGP103.2 billion ($3.34 billion) \\u2013 a 70-percent increase year-over-year.\\n\\nEzz's latest acquisition comes on the heels of a significant surge in Ezz Steel's share price on the Egyptian Exchange. Between Nov. 1 and 22, the market value of his existing stake climbed by EGP1.77 billion ($57.53 million), solidifying his position as both a leading investor on the bourse and one of the country's wealthiest individuals.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"86230\",\n    \"score\": 0.5301464796066284,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Ahmed Ezz takes direct controlling stake in Ezz Steel\\ndate: 2021-06-08\\n---\\n\\nAhmed Ezz now directly owns a controlling stake in Ezz Steel after purchasing a 33.4% stake in the company from El Ezz Group Holding for Industry and Investment, according to an EGX disclosure (pdf). The steel magnate, who owns almost 100% of Ezz Holding, now directly holds a 65.7% stake in Ezz Steel after purchasing almost 182 mn global depository receipts from the affiliated company. He has been a member of various musical groups and some of the earliest Pakistani rock bands like The Barbarians, Awaz, Karavan, Junoon, Vital Signs and Coke Studio Pakistan.\\n\\nEarly life\\n\\nHis family moved to Dubai when he was quite young. His elder brother was a guitarist and when he left for college, he left his guitar back at home. Asad picked it up and quickly learned to play. His family returned to Karachi in 1984.\\n\\nPersonal life\\n\\nOn 14 February 2019, Ahmed married Hira after dating her for two years. They got married in a nikah ceremony surrounded by close family and friends in Karachi.\\n\\nCareer\\n\\nCoke Studio (Pakistan)\\n\\nAsad played in Coke Studio (Produced by Rohail Hyatt) and was one of the house band members from season 2 (2008) to season 6 (2012) and reappeared in Season 13 in 2020. His style of guitar playing has some flashy showmanship in it.\\n\\nThe Barbarians\\n\\nAsad started his music career in 1987 with The Barbarians, which is regarded by many as Pakistan's first rock band. On Salman's invitation, he hopped on board with Junoon\"\n  }\n]"

With a total output of 5.14 million metric tonnes, Ezz Steel is far ahead of Saudi Arabia's Hadeed and Emirates Steel.\\n\\nPrior to the transaction, Ezz held a commanding 60.71-percent stake. Mineral Investment Development and El-Garhy Steel Group followed with 7.44 percent and 5.93 percent, respectively. The latest purchase strengthens Ezz's grip, solidifying his position as the group's dominant shareholder.\\n\\nEzz Steel dominates MENA market with stellar financial performance\\n\\nEzz Steel's financial performance in the first nine months of 2023 has been nothing short of impressive. Sales followed suit, surging from EGP60.6 billion ($1.96 billion) to EGP103.2 billion ($3.34 billion) \\u2013 a 70-percent increase year-over-year.\\n\\nEzz's latest acquisition comes on the heels of a significant surge in Ezz Steel's share price on the Egyptian Exchange. Most of his earnings stemmed from gains generated by his own capital invested in the fund. He received a small amount of fees as TCI had to hit its high-water mark before it could charge a performance fee.\\n\\nHohn is one of ten hedge fund managers who lost money in 2022 \\u2014 large sums in many cases \\u2014 but still wound up qualifying for the Rich List this year. Several of the ten are still below their high-water marks, including Tiger Global Management's Chase Coleman and Scott Shleifer and Perceptive Advisors' Joseph Edelman.\\n\\nThis is possible because under II's Rich List methodology, managers qualify in two ways: our calculation of gains from their personal capital in their funds and their share of the fees.\\n\\nOf course, a high-water mark is applied when calculating performance fees but is not applied to individuals' personal capital. Rather, the annual ranking is a snapshot in time. So whereas a manager may have lost a large amount of personal capital during a down year, he may still see that capital benefit when a fund goes up.\\n\\nAltogether, the 25 highest earners made a total of $26.085 billion. This works out to an average of $1.043 billion per person. The median earner made $750 million.\\n\\nAs a result, 2023 was the third-most-profitable year for the 25 highest earners, slightly behind the total in 2021. The best year was 2020, when the top 25 made a total of $31.71 billion. This year, 11 of the 25 made at least $1 billion.\\n\\nIn 2022,\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"56191\",\n    \"score\": 0.5174493193626404,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Egyptian billionaire Ahmed Ezz spends $11.1 million to boost stake in Ezz Steel\\nauthor: Omokolade Ajayi\\ndate: 2023-12-22\\n---\\nTable of Contents\\n\\nEgyptian billionaire businessman Ahmed Ezz, founder of leading steelmaker Ezz Steel, has further solidified his control over the company by snapping up additional shares in a deal worth EGP344 million ($11.1 million).\\n\\nThe transaction, brokered by Hermes Financial Group, saw Ezz acquire roughly 4.3 million shares at an average price of EGP80 ($2.59) per share from fellow Egyptian steel magnate Jamal El-Garhy \\u2014 this strengthens Ezz's position as the majority shareholder.\\n\\nLatest purchase strengthens Ezz's grip\\n\\nEzz Steel \\u2014 the largest independent steel producer in the Middle East and North Africa \\u2014 has delivered impressive financial results in recent times, further strengthening investors' interest and confidence. With a total output of 5.14 million metric tonnes, Ezz Steel is far ahead of Saudi Arabia's Hadeed and Emirates Steel.\\n\\nPrior to the transaction, Ezz held a commanding 60.71-percent stake. Mineral Investment Development and El-Garhy Steel Group followed with 7.44 percent and 5.93 percent, respectively. The latest purchase strengthens Ezz's grip, solidifying his position as the group's dominant shareholder.\\n\\nEzz Steel dominates MENA market with stellar financial performance\\n\\nEzz Steel's financial performance in the first nine months of 2023 has been nothing short of impressive. Profits soared to EGP27.9 billion ($883.1 million), a significant jump from the previous year's EGP22.1 billion ($709.6 million). Sales followed suit, surging from EGP60.6 billion ($1.96 billion) to EGP103.2 billion ($3.34 billion) \\u2013 a 70-percent increase year-over-year.\\n\\nEzz's latest acquisition comes on the heels of a significant surge in Ezz Steel's share price on the Egyptian Exchange. Between Nov. 1 and 22, the market value of his existing stake climbed by EGP1.77 billion ($57.53 million), solidifying his position as both a leading investor on the bourse and one of the country's wealthiest individuals.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"82113\",\n    \"score\": 0.5164241194725037,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Forbes World's Billionaires List 2023: The Top 200\\nauthor: Forbes Wealth Team\\ndate: 2023-07-07\\n---\\nFalling stocks, wounded unicorns and rising interest rates translated into a down year for the world's wealthiest people.\\n\\nGlobally, we counted 2,640 ten-figure fortunes, down from 2,668 last year. Altogether, the planet's billionaires are now worth $12.2 trillion, a drop of $500 billion from $12.7 trillion in March 2022. Nearly half the list is poorer than a year ago, including Elon Musk, who falls from No. 1 to No. 2 after his pricey acquisition of Twitter helped sink Tesla shares. Bernard Arnault, head of luxury goods giant LVMH, takes his place as the world's richest person, marking the first time a citizen of France leads the ranking.\\n\\nThe United States still boasts the most billionaires, with 735 list members worth a collective $4.5 trillion. China (including Hong Kong and Macau) remains second, with 562 billionaires worth $2 trillion, followed by India, with 169 billionaires worth $675 billion. To calculate net worths, we used stock prices and exchange rates from March 10, 2023. See below for the full list of the world's billionaires and our methodology. For daily updated net worths of all 2,640 billionaires, check out our real-time billionaires rankings.\\n\\nEdited by Rob LaFranco and Chase Peterson-Withorn.\\n\\n#1 | Bernard Arnault & family\\n\\nNet Worth: $211 Billion\\n\\nAge: 74\\n\\nCountry/Territory: France\\n\\nIndustry: Fashion & Retail\\n\\nOne of the world's ultimate taste-makers, Bernard Arnault oversees an empire of 70 brands including Louis Vuitton and Sephora.\\n\\n#2 | Elon Musk\\n\\nNet Worth: $180 Billion\\n\\nAge: 51\\n\\nCountry/Territory: United States\\n\\nIndustry: Automotive\\n\\nElon Musk is working to revolutionize transportation both on Earth, through electric car maker Tesla \\u2014 and in space, via rocket producer SpaceX.\\n\\n#3 | Jeff Bezos\\n\\nNet Worth: $114 Billion\\n\\nAge: 59\\n\\nCountry/Territory: United States\\n\\nIndustry: Technology\\n\\nJeff Bezos founded\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"85284\",\n    \"score\": 0.5158517956733704,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: In Memoriam: These Billionaires Died Over The Past Year\\nauthor: Aris Alexander\\ndate: 2023-04-05\\n---\\nEditor's Note: Forbes inadvertently left Tom Love, who died in March 2023, off of this post. Including Love, there were 29 billionaires who died over the past year.\\n\\nNotable three-comma club deaths include the founder of eyewear giant Luxottica and the cofounder of energy drink Red Bull.\\n\\nOfthe 287 people who fell off Forbes' World's Billionaires list in 2023, 29 lost their spot in the ranks because they died over the past year.\\n\\nThese tycoons, who include one of Malaysia's biggest bankers, an early Berkshire Hathaway backer and an Italian eyewear kingpin, hailed from 17 countries. They were worth a combined $147 billion, measured at the time of their death.\\n\\nOf the 29, 12 were U.S. citizens. The only other country to see multiple billionaires pass away was Austria, with two, including the wealthiest person to die since March 2022: Dietrich Mateschitz ($20.2 billion), who cofounded Red Bull and turned it into an energy drinks-sports marketing powerhouse.\\n\\nAn additional five billionaires dropped from the 2023 ranking, after appearing on the 2022 ranking, because Forbes discovered they had died prior to the 2022 list, meaning a total of 34 billionaires fell off the 2023 list because of death.\\n\\nHere are the billionaires who have died since the 2022 World's Billionaires list, listed in order of most recent to least recent:\\n\\nGordon Moore\\n\\nCitizenship: U.S. | Net worth at death: $6.8 bil | Died: March 2023, age 94\\n\\nA Caltech PhD in chemistry and physics, Moore was part of the \\\"traitorous eight\\\" that left Nobel Prize winner Bill Shockley's firm to found Fairchild Semiconductor in 1957. He cofounded Intel in 1968 and served as CEO from 1975 to 1987 and as chairman from 1979 to 1997. (He appears on the 2023 ranking because he died after Forbes finalized its list.)\\n\\nMasatoshi I\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"11199\",\n    \"score\": 0.5148887634277344,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: A Guide to the NFL Team Owners\\ndate: 2024-09-05\\n---\\nA Guide to the NFL Team Owners\\n\\nMeet the men and women who own the 32 teams in the NFL.\\n\\nEvery item on this page was chosen by a Town & Country editor. Ezz was enrolled in one of Egypt's leading international schools in the 1960s, and that had already guaranteed him an imbalanced playing field.\\n\\nThis would later on become a strong basis for the Egyptian public hating him \\u2013 or wishing they were him.\\n\\n\\\"With a curt wave of her hand, the wife of one of Egypt's richest men poses a question she already knows the answer to. The former minister allegedly allowed Ezz to illegally take over the state-owned Dekheila steel company.\\n\\nEzz was a prominent figure in former President Hosni Mubarak's now defunct NDP. He was head of the organisation committee and was the architect of the 2010 parliamentary elections that gave the party a 99 percent super majority.\\n\\nHe was also one of the closest allies to Mubarak's son, Gamal, and the two were viewed as the defining figures of the \\\"new guard\\\" within the party.\\n\\nThrough the policies committee of the party, of which the younger Mubarak was chairman and Ezz a member, the two steered the government into adopting aggressive neoliberal policies of free market capitalism, with the state selling off most of the companies nationalised in the 1960s by late President Gamal Abdel Nasser.\\n\\nDespite his advocacy for free market policies, Ezz, who was also a member of the lower house of parliament, the People's Assembly, has long been accused of holding a monopoly on the steel market.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"docid\": \"72355\",\n    \"score\": 0.6179916858673096,\n    \"snippet\": \"---\\ntitle: Ahmed Ezz - He has been a member of various musical groups and some of the earliest Pakistani rock bands like The Barbarians, Awaz, Karavan, Junoon, Vital Signs and Coke Studio Pakistan.\\n\\nEarly life\\n\\nHis family moved to Dubai when he was quite young. His elder brother was a guitarist and when he left for college, he left his guitar back at home. Asad picked it up and quickly learned to play. His family returned to Karachi in 1984.\\n\\nPersonal life\\n\\nOn 14 February 2019, Ahmed married Hira after dating her for two years. They got married in a nikah ceremony surrounded by close family and friends in Karachi.\\n\\nCareer\\n\\nCoke Studio (Pakistan)\\n\\nAsad played in Coke Studio (Produced by Rohail Hyatt) and was one of the house band members from season 2 (2008) to season 6 (2012) and reappeared in Season 13 in 2020. His style of guitar playing has some flashy showmanship in it.\\n\\nThe Barbarians\\n\\nAsad started his music career in 1987 with The Barbarians, which is regarded by many as Pakistan's first rock band. The band's first single \\\"Yeh Zindagi Hai\\\" (This is Life) set the foundation of Pakistani rock. \\n\\nThey released their only album, the self-titled \\\"The Barbarians\\\" in 1989 with the label EMI (Pakistan), which did not fare well in the then rock-repellant Pakistani music industry. The Barbarians band fell apart in 1990.\\n\\nJunoon and Vital Signs\\n\\nAsad did a gig with Salman Ahmad of Junoon at a party in 1991.
